title: 5 Tips for a GMAT Study Plan While Working Full-Time
description: Most GMAT advice assumes you have 4 hours a day free. Here are 5 realistic tips for building a plan around an actual full-time job.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: Most GMAT study guides are written for people with unlimited free time. Wake up at 6, study for 4 hours, take a break, study for 3 more. That's not realistic advice, that's advice for someone who isn't working a job.
If you're studying for the GMAT while working full-time, here's a plan built around the actual hours you have, not the hours a study guide wishes you had.

content.heading: Use your commute, don't waste it
list: If you commute by train or bus, that's 30-60 minutes of dead time, twice a day.
Use it for the lowest-effort review: flashcards, vocabulary, formula recall.
Save actual problem-solving for when you're at a desk, not swaying on a train.

content.heading: One good hour beats three tired ones
list: After a full workday, your brain is not at its sharpest. Don't schedule your hardest content for 9pm.
Pick one consistent hour, ideally right after work before you're fully drained, and protect it.
A single focused hour, four to five days a week, adds up to real progress over 8 to 10 weeks.

content.heading: Weekends carry the real weight
list: Weekday hours are for maintenance: keep skills sharp, don't lose ground.
Weekends are for the heavy lifting: full practice sections, timed sets, reviewing mistakes properly.
Two solid weekend sessions can outweigh five rushed weekday ones.

content.heading: Track time, not just questions solved
list: Working professionals often measure progress by "did I study today," which hides burnout building underneath.
Track actual focused minutes, not just a yes/no checkbox.
This makes it obvious when a week was genuinely light, instead of guessing.

content.heading: Give yourself one full day off, every week
list: This is the one people cut first when time is already tight, and the one that costs the most later.
Studying every single day while also working full-time is a fast route to quitting entirely around week 4.
One real day off keeps the whole plan sustainable for the 2 to 3 months this actually takes.

content.body: None of this requires quitting your job or finding hours that don't exist. It just means being honest about which hours you actually have, and using them well instead of pretending you have more.
